samples.summary: `ApiKeyService.list`/`revoke` default to the UNSCOPED (owner) scope when the caller omits it — a fail-open default on the boundary this PR just made load-bearing
samples.evidence: Until this PR the api-key surface was owner-only, so "no scope" meant the same thing everywhere. This PR makes creator-scoping the security boundary between members (docs/documentation/guide/workspaces.md now promises "See the list of API keys: Only the ones you created" and "Revoke an API key: Only ones you created"). The scope parameter is optional and defaults to `{}`: `async list(workspaceId: string, scope: KeyScope = {})` (api-key.service.ts:55) and `async revoke(id, workspaceId, scope: KeyScope = {})` (api-key.service.ts:92), where `{}` means "every key in the workspace". Today the only caller, `ApiKeyController.keyScope` (api-key.controller.ts:87-90), always computes a scope, so there is no live bypass — I confirmed with grep that `apiKeyService.list`/`revoke` have no other call site in packages/backend/src. But the default makes the insecure call the *shortest* one: any future caller (a background job, a new admin route, a refactor that drops the second argument) silently gets workspace-wide listing/revocation with no type error, and api-key.service.spec.ts:81/128 pins that behaviour as intended (`service.list('ws-1')` asserted to return every key). A required scope parameter (or `{ createdBy: number } | 'all'`) would make the owner case explicit and fail closed. Impact if it is ever hit: one member enumerating and revoking every other member's integration credentials.

samples.summary: Keys minted from the new member-facing UI always get full `['read','write']` scope and no expiry, with no per-member cap
samples.evidence: `createApiKey` in the frontend sends only `{ name }` (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:614), and the service defaults `scopes: scopes ?? ['read','write']` and `expiresAt: expiresAt ?? null` (api-key.service.ts:42-43). Before this PR only an owner could reach that path; the docs delta now advertises minting to every member, so every member of every workspace can self-issue an unlimited number of non-expiring, full-write bearer credentials from the browser. Each one is bounded by the minter's own authority (WorkspaceScopeGuard re-checks live membership, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard checks the write scope) and creation is behind the global ThrottlerGuard, so this is credential sprawl/hardening rather than escalation — a read-only default or an optional expiry in the create dialog would shrink the blast radius of a leaked key.
